actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 359 - 62 (Roll no. 24). (text: 1/21/2025 CR H248)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 359 - 62 (Roll no. 24). (text: 1/21/2025 CR H248)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H346)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 375.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H248-250)
Mr. Westerman moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.

Referred to the Committee on Natural Resources, and in addition to the Committee on Agriculture, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agency personnel, state forestry workers in Hawaii, landowners, and local stakeholders in control areas.
dimensions.evidence: partner with the Secretary of Agriculture, the State, and with local stakeholders to manage ungulates

dimensions.assessment: Directs ongoing scientific research, ungulate management, and forest restoration initiatives to control a destructive tree disease.
dimensions.evidence: prevent the spread of Rapid Ohia Death; and to restore the native forests of the State

dimensions.assessment: Requires the provision of financial assistance, staff, and infrastructure funding to research institutions, though specific dollar figures are unstated.
dimensions.evidence: provide financial assistance... and staff and necessary infrastructure funding

dimensions.assessment: Formalizes statutory collaboration and research mandates across specific federal and state entities regarding a plant pathogen.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of the Interior shall partner and collaborate with the Secretary of Agriculture and the State

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes sustained, ongoing scientific research and forest management efforts without a specified sunset date.
dimensions.evidence: shall continue to conduct research... shall continue to partner... shall continue to provide

missing_information: Exact amounts of financial assistance and infrastructure funding to be appropriated
Specific number of acres or personnel dedicated to the control areas
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates multi-agency collaboration and sustained research, ungulate management, and restoration efforts between the Department of the Interior, USDA, and Hawaii to combat Rapid Ohia Death. The impact is geographically concentrated in Hawaii and involves ongoing federal program coordination.
